scenario: AITA for expecting family time? | This morning I woke up and saw my husband watching video game streams, his typical pastime. Later he said the streamers he was watching were having cash giveaways that required participation to be entered. He continued to watch while he covertly built the kids' bikes in the garage as I had asked, then left to run a last-minute grocery errand for dinner, then came home and went upstairs to watch more streaming. After wrapping gifts, I did dishes and put dinner in the oven, and asked him to turn it off to spend time with me with/without kids. He said no. But if I was okay letting him spend $100 on app purchases for this game (same one he's watching) that he'd shut it off no problem. But last year he spent a little over $2,000 on in-app purchases for this game, and after a lengthy discussion, said he wouldn't buy anymore. So I'm not a huge fan of okaying any more money for it. It's almost 6pm and says he doesn't know when it will end, but that there are 2 more streamers left. I feel like the evening is almost over and I am so disappointed and feel saddened that he would rather watch games than spend time with me. Am I an asshole for being upset and having unrealistic expectations?

Scenario:
AITA for expecting family time? | This morning I woke up and saw my husband watching video game streams, his typical pastime. Later he said the streamers he was watching were having cash giveaways that required participation to be entered. He continued to watch while he covertly built the kids' bikes in the garage as I had asked, then left to run a last-minute grocery errand for dinner, then came home and went upstairs to watch more streaming. After wrapping gifts, I did dishes and put dinner in the oven, and asked him to turn it off to spend time with me with/without kids. He said no. That the stream was only for today and it is not okay for me to expect him to stop doing what he finds enjoyable just because I want him to do something I find enjoyable. But if I was okay letting him spend $100 on app purchases for this game (same one he's watching) that he'd shut it off no problem. But last year he spent a little over $2,000 on in-app purchases for this game, and after a lengthy discussion, said he wouldn't buy anymore. So I'm not a huge fan of okaying any more money for it. It's almost 6pm and says he doesn't know when it will end, but that there are 2 more streamers left. I feel like the evening is almost over and I am so disappointed and feel saddened that he would rather watch games than spend time with me. Am I an asshole for being upset and having unrealistic expectations?

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: Based on the scenario, I would say that you are not an asshole (NTA - Not The Asshole). Here's why: 1. **You had a clear request**: You asked your husband to turn off the stream and spend time with you, which is a reasonable request considering the evening is almost over and you've been busy with household chores. 2. **He had a history of prioritizing gaming**: Your husband has a history of spending a significant amount of money on in-app purchases for the game, which suggests that gaming is a priority for him. This history makes his current behavior more understandable, but not necessarily justifiable. 3. **You're not asking him to give up gaming entirely**: You're not asking your husband to stop gaming altogether; you're asking him to prioritize spending time with you and the kids for a few hours in the evening. 4. **He's being inconsistent**: Your husband is saying that he won't stop gaming because you're asking him to, but he's willing to stop gaming if you're okay with him spending $100 on in-app purchases. This inconsistency suggests that he's not taking your feelings and needs into account. 5. **You're feeling disappointed and saddened**: Your feelings are valid, and it's okay to feel disappointed and saddened when your partner prioritizes something else over spending time with you. It's essential to communicate your feelings and needs with your husband in a clear and respectful manner. You might say something like, "I feel disappointed and saddened when you prioritize gaming over spending time with me and the kids. I understand that you enjoy gaming, but I feel like we need to find a balance between our individual interests and our family time. Can we discuss ways to prioritize our family time and make sure we're both happy and fulfilled?" Remember, communication is key in any relationship, and it's essential to work together to find a balance that works for both partners.
